name: SUNDAY MORNING COMICS
notes: Beetle only enlisted in March 1951 and Camp Swampy came after, so 'since 1950' was wrong — date dropped; Blondie 1930, Dick Tracy's wrist radio and Garfield all check.

name: THE FUNNY PAGES
notes: Its $400 Peanuts answer twinned the adjacent category's Snoopy clue (both naming Charlie Brown) — moved Popeye to $400 and added Li'l Abner/Dogpatch/Sadie Hawkins at $1200; still a topic sibling of SUNDAY MORNING COMICS, now with no shared strip.

name: THE STORYBOOK MENAGERIE
notes: Clifford/Emily Elizabeth, Charlotte the barn spider, Babar's green suit and Munro Leaf's Ferdinand all correct; character-name gimmick stays distinct from the species category.

name: WHAT KIND OF ANIMAL?
notes: Paddington, Bambi, Black Beauty, Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle and Rikki-Tikki-Tavi verified; 'fawn' is a conceivable stray response on the Bambi row, and Potter is echoed in DRAWN BY HAND.

name: DRAWN BY HAND
notes: Its $400 Norman Rockwell duplicated the same pack's finals clue (ef-wave4 NEWSSTAND NOSTALGIA), same Saturday Evening Post fact — swapped in Dr. Seuss and the Cat's striped hat; Carle, Sendak 1963 and Scarry verified.

name: THAT CAME FROM A BOOK
notes: Dropped the 'Dr. Seuss' mention from the Grinch clue (he is now an answer one category away) and dated the Grinch to 1957; Frankenstein 1818, Orwell and Heller 1961 all correct.

name: STORYTELLERS WE GREW UP WITH
notes: Its $400 Laura Ingalls Wilder duplicated the same pack's finals clue (ef-wave4 PIONEER GIRL), Little House fact and all — replaced with Mark Twain; Grahame's Scottish birth and banking career verified.

name: THE SCHOOL LIBRARY SHELF
notes: Nancy Drew's blue roadster, Bayport, Old Yeller, Klickitat Street and Encyclopedia Brown's 25-cents-a-day fee in Idaville all confirmed.

name: THE PULL-DOWN MAP
notes: Equator, Australia, Panama Canal 1914, Continental Divide and Date Line all correct and gently pitched; only Australia overlaps a Fresh-pack answer.

name: THE HISTORY LESSON
notes: Its $800 Ellis Island repeated the same pack's finals clue (ef-wave4 THE GOLDEN DOOR) nearly word for word — replaced with the 1773 Boston Tea Party; Betsy Ross stays properly hedged as legend.

name: IN YOUR BEST HANDWRITING
notes: Reworded the $1600 so the answer is the blotter pad rather than 'blotting paper'; inkwell desks, quill, Hancock and nib are all solid and warmly nostalgic.

name: MIND YOUR GRAMMAR
notes: Scored 43 as written — flat ladder of dictionary definitions with a $2000 no harder than the $400; dropped the adjective row, moved conjunction and preposition down and added a semicolon clue so the rows actually climb.
